instruction: You are a strategic corporate innovation advisor conducting a reassessment. Analyse the prior assessment summary, changes since last assessment, and updated survey, then respond with a complete reassessment JSON including score_delta, carry_forward, progress, and comparison_to_previous.

answers.companyDescription: Generic drug manufacturer producing oral solid dosage forms (tablets, capsules) across 8 therapeutic categories. EU GMP-certified manufacturing facility with capacity for 2 billion tablets annually. Currently investing in continuous manufacturing line technology to replace batch processing for high-volume products. We have a dedicated management team across core functions but operate with limited middle management layers. Budget cycles are annual with moderate flexibility for mid-year reallocation if a strong business case is presented. Innovation initiatives compete with day-to-day operational demands for team attention.
answers.pastInitiatives: Innovation is embedded in our operating rhythm. We run quarterly hackathons, maintain a formal patent portfolio, and have a rotating 'innovation fellow' program where high-potential employees spend 6 months dedicated to exploratory projects. Our last hackathon produced a prototype for automated quality inspection using computer vision that is now in production, reducing defect escape rate by 35%.
answers.strategicGoals: Our primary objective is to reduce operating expenses by 15% over the next 2 years while maintaining current output levels. We believe there is significant waste in our manual processes and want to identify the highest-ROI automation opportunities across order processing, invoicing, and customer support workflows. We are not looking to grow headcount — we want to do more with our existing team.
answers.teamSize: We have a small technology team of 4-8 people including developers, a part-time DevOps engineer, and a product manager who also handles project management. The team is fully allocated to maintaining current products and handling integration requests from key clients. Innovation work is done in the margins — there is no formally ring-fenced innovation time or budget.
answers.additionalContext: We completed a merger with a similarly-sized competitor 4 months ago and are in the middle of integrating teams, systems, and processes. The combined organization has significant duplication — two CRMs, two HR systems, overlapping product lines. There is a unique window to redesign processes from scratch rather than patching legacy approaches, but cultural integration is fragile and change fatigue is real.

input.changes_since_last: Hired 6 new team members. Launched customer feedback pilot. Budget for innovation increased 25%.

opportunities.title: Harmonization of Core Business Processes Post-Merger
opportunities.rationale: The merger presents a unique, time-sensitive opportunity to move beyond 'patching' legacy systems and redesign core workflows (order processing, invoicing, support) from scratch. This is the highest ROI area for achieving the 15% expense reduction goal by eliminating duplicated efforts and streamlining manual processes.

first_actions: Establish a cross-functional Governance Committee including representation from both legacy companies' operations, IT, Legal, and Quality Assurance to define new state processes (Compliance first).
Map current 'as-is' processes for the top 3 high-volume workflows (e.g., order-to-cash) across all systems identified.
Develop standardized SOPs and training materials that integrate compliance checks at every process stage, satisfying EU GMP requirements.
resources_needed: IT System Architect (for future state design)
execution_plan.success_metric: Reduction in average cycle time for order processing and invoicing by 20%.
milestones: Completion of 'as-is' process mapping for core workflows.
Final approval of the 'to-be' integrated process model by governance committee.
Pilot implementation of redesigned flow in a single department/product line.

opportunities.title: Systemizing and Scaling AI/CV Insights Across Production Lines
opportunities.rationale: The success of the automated quality inspection prototype proves internal capability. This opportunity focuses on formalizing the deployment and expansion of successful technological prototypes (like CV) into other high-defect, manual areas to drive measurable operational savings.

first_actions: Conduct a detailed cost-benefit analysis comparing current defect rates/manual inspection time vs. automation capability for 3 adjacent production processes.
Formalize the tech team's capacity by ring-fencing 20% of their time specifically for scaling and integration efforts, shielding it from immediate operational maintenance demands.
Update SOPs to include standardized data capture protocols required for ongoing AI/ML model training.
Conduct GDPR and data privacy compliance review with legal team to ensure alignment with applicable regulations
resources_needed: Dedicated Process Engineer (to identify expansion points)
execution_plan.success_metric: Increased automation coverage from 1 process line to 3+ lines, achieving a cumulative defect escape rate reduction of 10%.
milestones: Selection and technical scoping of the next two target processes.
Successful integration and testing of automated inspection in the second location.
Creation of a repeatable 'automation deployment playbook'.

next_steps.action: Draft and secure executive sign-off for the 'New Operating Model' Governance Charter to legitimize process redesign efforts across both merged entities.
Schedule a resource allocation meeting with key department heads to formally commit time and budget (even if small) for the dedicated tech scaling efforts, protecting it from day-to-day demands.
Move beyond NPS surveys by hosting deep-dive interviews with the top 10 highest value, most complained-to customers to qualify pain points for automation/process redesign.

key_weaknesses: Significant organizational complexity and duplication arising from the recent merger (two CRMs, two HR systems).
Lack of protected time or budget for innovation, forcing initiatives to compete with immediate operational demands.
Fragile cultural integration and high change fatigue across middle management layers.

improvements: Successful creation and deployment of a Computer Vision automated quality inspection system in production (35% defect reduction).
Formalizing the innovation rhythm with structured activities like quarterly hackathons and dedicated fellow programs.
Increased budget allocation for innovation by 25%, demonstrating renewed executive commitment.
persistent_gaps: Systemic process inefficiency remains high due to lack of integrated workflows across merged systems.
The technology team is severely bottlenecked between maintaining legacy products and handling new client integration requests.
A unified, single source of truth for operational data (CRM/ERP) has not been established.
achieved_milestones: Prototype automation successfully moved to production scale in QA inspection.
Increased visibility into customer pain points through the NPS survey methodology.

comparison_to_previous.key_changes: The company moved from merely having 'formal' processes to actively implementing successful tech prototypes and initiating process redesign following a major merger. The key shift is the window of opportunity presented by the merger to execute radical systemic improvements.
